newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian real drops 0.07 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian real drops 0.07 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.07 percent to close at 1.0738 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank lowered the real-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
The Central Bank depreciated the mini-band Thursday for the third time this month, lowering it 0.09 percent to between 1.0730 and 1.0780 reais per dollar through a buy/sell auction.
The previous mini-band was set on Monday at between 1.0720 and 1.0770 per dollar.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.28 percent against the dollar compared to an average monthly drop of between 0.57 and 0.63 percent in the past six months.

The real's fall was also due to net dollar outflows, dealers said. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts at 1650 local time/1950 GMT Thursday showed a $130 million deficit. On Wednesday, forex contracts posted a $142.3 million deficit.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed steady at 1.0776 per dollar.
In the parallel market, the real closed unchanged at 1.125 per greenback.
